answer: The kernel test I would run is Proof of unique organ donor registry entry: a registry entry held for a decade, so each new name must bring its own proof instead of reusing a sibling's. A farm that reuses one proof across ten accounts is caught at the second account, because a registry entry held for a decade is bound to a single identity — the ripple is that reuse itself becomes the evidence. Running a hundred clones would mean a hundred separate proofs, each costing real money and real time, and the plume of that bill is larger than anything one epoch pays out.
